discrepancies.title: Rent roll totals do not equal the sum of its rows: annual rent

sources.label: sum of unit rows: annual rent

discrepancies.why: The stated total is not the sum of the unit rows (it may be stale or typed over). The screen re-sums the rows and ignores the stated totals.

impact.basis: sum of rows minus stated total

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the property manager for a system export of the rent roll at the same date.

discrepancies.title: 3 unit(s) marked occupied with leases that ended before 2026-11-01 (208, 212, 404); 2 let unit(s) with no Ejari number (211, 312)
discrepancies.why: A tenant holding over on an expired or unregistered lease has a weaker legal position for the landlord (an unregistered contract lacks legal standing). The engine rolls expired leases at the start of the analysis; AED 369,000 of in-place rent (13.5%) sits on these units.

impact.basis: in-place rent on the affected units

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request Ejari certificates and renewal status for each listed unit.

discrepancies.title: Statement rental income AED 2,331,125 is 15.0% below rent-roll in-place rent AED 2,742,500
discrepancies.why: Physical occupancy is not economic occupancy: units on the roll are not paying in full (arrears, concessions, bounced cheques or tenants not paying). The screen therefore underwrites income at what is actually collected, a collection loss of 15.0% instead of the mandate's 1.0% (amounts are for a 12-month period).

impact.basis: rent-roll in-place rent minus statement rental income

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the aged receivables report and bank statements for the statement period.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 8.8% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 1,921,461 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 8.3%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 134,175 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 37% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 41% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 22% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).

rejected_model_findings.title: OM headline rent appears to equal full-building rent although 8% of units are said to be vacant
rejected_model_findings.why: The OM gives a single 'Total Rent (Yearly)' of AED 2,742,000 without saying it is contracted rent of let units, and says the building is only 92% occupied. The parsed rent roll shows in-place rent equal to potential rent (AED 2,742,500), which suggests vacant, notice-served or legal-case units may carry rent in the total. The 8.8% ROI is calculated on this figure, so it may present potential rent as current income. The T12 statement shows lower cash income, which supports this concern.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Ask the broker for a unit-by-unit schedule showing which units' rent is included in the AED 2,742,000 figure. Confirm that vacant, notice-served and legal-case units are excluded from in-place rent. Recompute yield on contracted rent of occupied units with valid Ejari.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: contradicted by the rent roll: OM income AED 2,742,000 equals in-place rent AED 2,742,500 within 2%

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the building passes every hard mandate filter but misses four soft tests (going-in yield on total cost, unlevered IRR, unlevered equity multiple and minimum occupancy) at the asking price.

Buy at AED 20.1m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 35% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]], against an asking price of AED 31.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the exit yield: a swing of 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either way moves it by AED 3.4m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Opaline Residence, Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC), 48 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2012 [[deal.completion_year]], freehold single title.
- **Price:** AED 31.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], or AED 965 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA.
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 2.7m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on direct leases with no master tenant. The rent roll shows 92% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units. After the screen rolls expired leases, occupancy is 88% [[uw.occupancy_by_units]]. The largest expiry window, between 1 November 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]], holds 37% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent.

## Returns
| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR, pre-tax | 0.0% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] (a marginal loss) | at least 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Unlevered equity multiple | 1.00x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | at least 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 5.0% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 4.7% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | at least 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |

Year-1 NOI is AED 1.5m [[uw.noi_year1]].

Levered, pre-tax: a loss of 3.2% a year [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] and an equity multiple of 0.86x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's 8.8% [[om.yield_stated]] headline yield is on asking price, with no stated income basis. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 4.7% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The buyer's yield is below the OM's figure: the gap is negative, 4.1 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]].

## What would make it fail
- **Exit yield:** with the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is a loss of 1.2% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **No grid case gets close:** the best case has market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter. Unlevered IRR is 2.8% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], well under the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target.
- **Collections:** the operating statement shows far less rent than the rent roll (see Discrepancies). If the shortfall is arrears, income is lower than the roll implies.
- **Expiries:** the AED 974k [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] expiring in the first window meets a house view in which market rent falls 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1.

## Discrepancies
Most severe first. Lower-severity items are not discussed.
1. **Rent roll does not foot (high).** The stated rent total is not the sum of the unit rows. The screen used the unit rows and ignored the stated totals.
2. **Expired or unregistered leases shown as occupied (high).** Three units marked occupied have leases that ended before the rent roll date, and two let units have no Ejari number. AED 369,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]] of in-place rent (13.5% [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]]) sits on these units. The landlord's legal position is weaker. The screen rolls the expired leases at the start of the analysis.
3. **Collections gap (high).** Statement rental income is AED 2.3m [[opex.rental_income]], against AED 2.7m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] of in-place rent on the roll. The screen underwrites a collection loss of 15% [[disc.collections_gap.observed_gap]] instead of the mandate's 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The roll overstates collected income by AED 411k [[disc.collections_gap.impact_aed]].
4. **OM yield before acquisition costs (medium).** The OM's 8.8% [[om.yield_stated]] is before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]]. On price plus costs, the OM's own income gives 8.3% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]]. This is the same gap as the OM-versus-buyer yield comparison above, counted once.

## Checks before diligence
- Get a system export of the rent roll at the same date from the property manager.
- Get Ejari certificates and renewal status for each flagged unit.
- Get the aged receivables report and bank statements for the statement period.
- Ask the broker to restate the yield on total cost.
- Security deposits of AED 134k [[uw.security_deposits_aed]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile: 22% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on six or more cheques, which means more collection risk.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.

## Assumptions
House view: exit yield of 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]], which includes 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion plus an age premium. Market rent falls 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then rises 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]], renewal probability is 70% [[assume.renewal_probability]], and the hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. Debt is a loan of AED 10.2m [[uw.loan_aed]] at 33% [[uw.ltv]] LTV and a 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] rate, sized to a 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
